objective: Design how holyagent's Claude Code plugin ships fff (github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff) as a required MCP server that every holyagent agent must use for file search and content search, working in claude.ai cloud sessions and on darwin-arm64, linux-x64 and windows-x64.

result: Ship fff by pinning v0.11.0 and downloading the bare `fff-mcp-<target>` binary at runtime into `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`. A bundled `holyagent fff-mcp` launcher does the download and SHA-256 check, a plugin-level stdio MCP entry runs it, and agents lose Grep and Glob by denylist. Cloud support for the holyagent plugin itself is unverified.

## Sourced facts

**npm and bunx**
- fff ships no npm package that runs the MCP server. The npm packages are SDKs: `@ff-labs/fff-node` and `@ff-labs/fff-bun` (0.11.0, https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ff-labs/fff-bun). The README lists the MCP server only as a binary: install script, Homebrew, or the release binary (https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff).
- `bunx fff download` and `bunx fff info` (in the fff-bun package) fetch the FFI library, not `fff-mcp`.
- A third-party directory (syncdev.com) lists `npx -y @ff-labs/fff-node` as an MCP command. I could not verify it, and it is an SDK package, so I do not recommend it.
- The repo moved from `fff.nvim` to `fff`. v0.11.0 was published 2026-09-21 (https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/releases/tag/v0.11.0).

**install-mcp.sh**
- URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/main/install-mcp.sh. It pins `PINNED_RELEASE_TAG="v0.11.0"` and per-target SHA-256 values.
- It downloads `https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/releases/download/<tag>/fff-mcp-<target>[.exe]`. Linux maps to musl targets.
- It verifies with `sha256sum -c`, installs to `~/.local/bin`, and prints `claude mcp add -s user fff -- <path>`. Its project `.mcp.json` snippet is `{"mcpServers":{"fff":{"type":"stdio","command":"fff-mcp","args":[]}}}`.

**Pinned checksums (v0.11.0, from install-mcp.sh)**

| Platform | Release asset | SHA-256 | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| linux-x64 | `fff-mcp-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` | `d1e8671f40c89c445aaa1728a21ec04b74be2e5f99091485caeabcc97f99aceb` | 12.7 MB |
| darwin-arm64 | `fff-mcp-aarch64-apple-darwin` | `cc606d9418cfa7764376dcd7b32a33e6459a6cb9a4718be366b024dca6e9fead` | 7.0 MB |
| windows-x64 | `fff-mcp-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` | `7a40439b06a33880487661b519f116a6a6d48b1c684bce79adfd5666875f23fd` | 13.9 MB |

- The same script also pins darwin-x64 `33377a8f…e862`, linux-arm64-musl `35f8e05d…577d` and windows-arm64 `6525ac80…ced`.
- Release assets are listed in the release page above. I could not fetch the `.sha256` files because Exa rejects the content type. The checksums above therefore rest on one source, so the root should cross-check them against the release `.sha256` files.

**fff-mcp binary** (source: `crates/fff-mcp/src/main.rs` at tag v0.11.0)
- Tools are `grep`, `find_files` and `multi_grep`. The README ("The MCP tools are grep, find_files, and multi_grep") and the server's built-in instructions agree. The older `ffgrep`, `fffind` and `fff-multi-grep` names in the DeepWiki page and in older README text are stale.
- Flags include `[PATH]`, `--no-update-check`, `--frecency-db`, `--log-file`, `--healthcheck`, `--no-watch` and `--idle-timeout-secs`.
- It indexes the git root discovered from its working directory, or from `PATH` if given.
- It exits when its parent process dies.
- It runs an update check at startup unless `--no-update-check` is passed.

**Plugin MCP declaration** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)
- A plugin declares MCP servers in `.mcp.json` at the plugin root or inline in `plugin.json`.
- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` substitute in stdio `command`, `args` and `env`, and are exported to the server process.
- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` resolves to `~/.claude/plugins/data/{id}/`, survives plugin updates, and is created on first reference.
- Plugin servers start automatically when the plugin is enabled.
- `alwaysLoad: true` on a server keeps its tools out of tool-search deferral. It needs Claude Code v2.1.121 or later (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.121).
- Startup retries up to 3 times on a transient error (same release note).

**Tool names for subagents** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, retrieved through search highlights)
- The full form is `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`. With plugin `holyagent` and server key `fff`, the tools are `mcp__plugin_holyagent_fff__grep`, `__find_files` and `__multi_grep`. The server key `fff` is my choice, and the plugin name follows from `PLUGIN_NAME`.
- Use this full name in permission rules, a subagent's `tools` field and hook matchers. A hook matcher written against the bare server key never fires for a plugin server.

**Subagents and MCP tools** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)
- Subagents inherit MCP tools.
- A background subagent keeps every MCP tool but only a fixed list of built-ins, and that list includes `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash` and `ToolSearch`.
- `disallowedTools` is applied first and then `tools` is resolved against what remains. It accepts `mcp__server`, `mcp__server__*` and `mcp__*` entries.
- Plugin agents ignore the frontmatter fields `mcpServers`, `hooks` and `permissionMode` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components).

**Grep and Glob on macOS, Linux and WSL** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference)
- On macOS, Linux and WSL, Grep and Glob are absent by default. Claude searches through Bash `find` and `grep`, which are embedded `bfs` and `ugrep`.
- They come back for a subagent that lists them in `tools` without Bash.
- Denying Grep and Glob therefore does not stop shell searching. It does bind on Windows and in agents that have no Bash.

**Hook timing** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, plus anthropics/claude-code issue #51148)
- `.mcp.json` is read once at startup, before any SessionStart hook.
- A SessionStart hook download therefore cannot supply the binary for the first session.
- The download has to happen inside the MCP `command` itself.

**claude.ai and cloud support**
- Plugins with a top-level `bin/` "Can't be installed" on chat and Cowork, and a local MCP server is "Ignored" in chat (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/platform-support).
- The same page says that "on the web, the plugin's Connectors tab marks [a local MCP server] Runs in each session." The page's installation table covers account plugins and does not mention cloud sessions.
- A claude.ai-account plugin appears in Claude Code as a synced plugin at the next session start (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/overview).
- Cloud sessions do not load plugins enabled in the repo's `.claude/settings.json` or on the user's machine (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/install and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments). Only server-managed org plugins are documented as reaching them (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org).
- A repo `.mcp.json` does load in a single-repository cloud session.
- The cloud VM is Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64.
- Trusted network access allows `github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com` and `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`. The `None` level blocks them.

## Design

1. **Binary**
   - Add a bundled CLI command `holyagent fff-mcp`, written in Effect with tagged errors, using `fetch`, `Bun.CryptoHasher` and Bun `$` or spawn.
   - A source constant holds the tag `v0.11.0` and the target-to-SHA-256 table above.
   - The launcher runs these steps:
     1. Pick the target from `process.platform` and `process.arch`, and fail with a tagged error for an unsupported pair.
     2. Look for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/fff/v0.11.0/fff-mcp-<target>[.exe]` and reuse it if present.
     3. Otherwise download the asset to a pid-named temp file in the same directory.
     4. Compare its SHA-256 with the pinned value and delete the file on mismatch.
     5. Rename it into place and `chmod 755` on non-Windows.
     6. Spawn it with inherited stdio, forward its exit code, and write all logs to stderr only.
   - Bump the version by editing the constant.

2. **MCP declaration**
   - Generate `dist/.mcp.json` in `generate.ts`, next to `hooks()` and `manifests()`.
   - Preferred form: `{"mcpServers":{"fff":{"type":"stdio","command":"bun","args":["--no-env-file","--config=${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/empty-bunfig.toml","${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/holyagent.js","fff-mcp"],"alwaysLoad":true}}}`.
   - The launcher passes `--no-update-check` to fff-mcp and may pass `--frecency-db`.
   - I chose `bun` as the command because the extensionless `scripts/holyagent` sh wrapper may not spawn as an MCP command on native Windows. The wrapper already works for hooks, but I have no source for MCP. This is an inference to test.
   - Because `bun` is resolved on PATH here, the wrapper's `$HOME/.bun/bin` fallback does not apply.
   - There is no `bin/` directory, so the claude.ai bin/ rejection does not apply.

3. **Agent rules**
   - In `agents.ts`, remove `Grep` and `Glob` from the `granted` list in `builtinsOf` and from `ROOT_BUILTINS`. The `denylist` function then puts them into every `disallowedTools` line.
   - Add no `tools:` line, because inheriting MCP tools is the current design.
   - Add a shared specialist section and a root section saying that all file search and content search uses `mcp__plugin_holyagent_fff__grep`, `__find_files` and `__multi_grep`.
   - Replace the "Locate with Grep and Glob" phrase in `roles/explorer-lookup/method.md` and its `R-EL` entry in `REQUIREMENT_SECTIONS`.
   - For roles that keep Bash, a PreToolUse hook on `Bash` with an `if` rule such as `Bash(*grep*)` could add a context-only reminder, matching the existing hook style. A hard deny would change the hooks' "context only" rule, so that is the root's decision.
   - If the fff tools are missing, agents report a blocker to the root.

4. **Files that change**
   - `packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts`: emit `.mcp.json`.
   - `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts`: tool lists and `REQUIREMENT_SECTIONS`.
   - New `packages/runtime/src/cli/fff-mcp.ts` for the launcher, registered with the other commands. I did not read `main.ts`, so I do not know where commands are registered.
   - `packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/`: the specialist and root sections plus `roles/explorer-lookup/method.md`.
   - `packages/integrations/claude/tests/plugin.test.ts`: the test at line 408 ("each role keeps exactly its previous built-in tools") and any `.mcp.json` assertion.
   - Regenerate `dist/` with `mise run build`.
   - Optionally `packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts` for a Bash reminder. Do not put the download in the `session-start` hook (see the hook-timing fact above).

## Conflicts and limits
- Tool names: the older README and DeepWiki (`ffgrep`, `fffind`, `fff-multi-grep`) conflict with the v0.11.0 source and the current README (`grep`, `find_files`, `multi_grep`). I follow the source.
- Old GitHub issues report that subagents cannot see MCP tools. They cover versions around 2.1.84, background subagents, and issue #53865 (wildcard in `tools` unrecognized). The current docs say they inherit, and holyagent already depends on inherited Exa tools. A live test is still advisable.
- I could not confirm that the holyagent plugin loads in a claude.ai cloud session, or that agents and hooks work there. The repo's directory marketplace does not load in cloud. A cloud session needs the plugin installed through the claude.ai account or server-managed settings.
- Because each cloud VM is fresh, the download likely repeats every session (inference). Whether `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` persists in a cloud VM is unverified.
- A first-run download inside MCP startup may exceed the 30-second `MCP_TIMEOUT`, a figure from a secondary issue report (#104418). Startup retries up to 3 times.
- A musl binary on a glibc machine should run because it is static (inference).
- On Apple silicon, running a downloaded unsigned binary may need a code signature. Unverified.

questions: Should denial of shell-based grep, `find` and `rg` be a hard hook deny, or reminder only? Should the fallback when fff is unavailable be a blocker report, or a Bash search?
